title: Upgrade orchestration index and smoke-probe checklist for Terraform modules/providers in Private VPC
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Create a compact, readable orchestration index (compatibility grid + safe pin recommendations) and a deployable smoke-probe checklist for Terraform module and provider upgrades that target Private VPC deployments. Goal is to reduce rollout incidents and provide on-call engineers with an actionable sequence of validations that can be run pre- and post-upgrade. Scope: terraform root modules used in private-vpc repo, providers used across our on-prem and VPC pipelines (aws, google, azurerm, random, tls, kubernetes), and our internal helper modules (vpc-bootstrap, rg-provisioner, k8s-nodepool). Deliverables: 1) human-readable upgrade index (CSV/markdown table) listing tested-from -> tested-to pairs, known failure modes, mitigation steps, and preferred pin. 2) Smoke-probe checklist (runnable steps with expected success criteria and telemetry queries). 3) Small automation helpers: terraform plan gate script and a provider sanity probe that runs post-apply and emits a compact report. 4) Rollback playbook skeleton and emergency contacts. Success metric: 50% reduction in manual rollback incidents for tf upgrades across Private VPC within next two cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade index committed to infra-docs (markdown) and validated by infra-runbook owner
Smoke-probe checklist documented and executable by SRE with <= 10 minutes overhead
Provider pin recommendations included in module README and enforced via CI gate for at least two modules
Automation helpers merged behind feature flag and tested on canary account
Runbook includes explicit rollback steps and links to the latest cluster-state dashboards
migration_matrix_examples: vpc-bootstrap module v1.3.2 -> v1.4.0: provider hashicorp/aws 4.12.0 -> 4.18.1: STATUS=compatible; NOTE=IAM policy arns handling changed, add dry-run to smoke-probe step #3
rg-provisioner module v0.9.0 -> v1.0.0: provider hashicorp/azurerm 3.2.1 -> 3.8.0: STATUS=partial; NOTE=resource address renames require state-mv in upgrade playbook
k8s-nodepool module v2.0.1 -> v2.1.0: provider hashicorp/kubernetes 2.11.0 -> 2.13.0: STATUS=compatible; NOTE=verify kubectl version compatibility in probe
root-private-vpc.tf: terraform 1.4.6 -> 1.5.0: STATUS=unknown; ACTION=run module-dependent acceptance tests in canary before pin change
provider hashicorp/random 3.x -> 4.x: STATUS=breaking; MITIGATION=pin to 3.x until dependent modules adopt new API
rollout_plan: 1) Publish upgrade index draft to infra-docs and notify SRE/Platform teams for review (2 business days)
2) Pick one low-risk module (vpc-bootstrap) in canary org and run full upgrade flow end-to-end
3) Execute smoke-probe pre-upgrade, apply changes with feature-flagged helper, run smoke-probe post-upgrade
4) If probe passes, flip pins in central module registry and open targeted PRs for downstream repos
5) Monitor telemetry for 72 hours; if errors increase > 5x baseline in any critical metric, trigger rollback playbook
6) Iterate on index entries and promote to majority modules once two canary upgrades succeed
smoke_probe_checklist: Pre-upgrade: run 'tf plan -out=plan.out' and generate human-readable diff; abort if drift > expected
Pre-upgrade: run automated acceptance suite against staging (networking and IAM focused)
Apply: feature-flagged CI job that calls 'terraform apply -auto-approve plan.out' into canary account
Post-apply probe #1: API health check - confirm control-plane endpoints return 200 within 500ms
Post-apply probe #2: Resource reconciliation - run 'terraform refresh' and confirm no unknowns
Post-apply probe #3: Workload smoke - deploy small test pod and hit end-to-end path (logs, metrics emitted)
Decision gate: all probes green OR documented rationale with SPO approval to proceed
automation_helpers: tf-plan-gate.sh: CI script to validate that plan changes do not touch pinned provider constraints
provider-sanity-probe.py: lightweight probe that validates provider RPCs used by modules (create/list/delete test resources in canary namespace)
index-gen.py (optional): generates index report from our test runs and tags entries with 'canary-passed'
feature-flag toggles to control helper execution in production runs
